title: Harness integrated data curation and stochastic eval scheduler for reproducible profile generation
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Model onboarding requires consistent, repeatable performance profiles published to the model catalog. Current harness runs are brittle: dataset sampling is ad-hoc, prompt templates diverge between eval runners, and nondeterministic sampling makes profile results hard to reproduce. This ticket implements an integrated data curation pipeline inside the benchmark harness plus a stochastic eval scheduler that records seeds, shards, and sampling metadata so performance profiles are reproducible and traceable across model versions. The work spans dataset selection/annotation, prompt templatization, runner orchestration, CI gating, and profile artifact publishing.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can register and persist curated dataset manifests with canonical sampling seeds and shard mappings.
Eval runners accept a unified eval_config that includes sampling_strategy, seed, shard_id, and prompt_template_version.
Stochastic eval scheduler can run N randomized repeats for an eval scenario and produce a merged performance profile with confidence intervals.
Generated performance profile artifacts (metrics + deterministic provenance) are published to the profile registry with semantic versioning and signed artifact metadata.

End-to-end reproducibility: given profile artifact metadata, re-running the harness with --replay should produce bit-for-bit identical micro-benchmarks (within nondeterministic GPU noise bounds) and identical aggregated metrics.

CI job added that validates new profile artifacts against the previous release for regressions in latency/p99 and token-cost with an automated alert and blocking capability for significant regressions.
implementation_notes: Add curated dataset manifest format: fields = dataset_id, split, canonical_seed, sampling_strategy, filters, provenance_url.
Implement DatasetRegistry in harness: S3-backed manifests + local cache; simple contract to produce deterministic iterators when given a seed and shard count.
Extend prompt templating: prompt_template_version field, and a linting step that ensures stable tokenization for common tokenizers (GPT-like, LLaMA-like).
Create stochastic eval scheduler component: takes eval_config and orchestrates repeated runs using different RNG seeds; records per-run metadata into the profile envelope.
Define unified eval_config schema (yaml/json) for runners: include model_version_pin, batch_shapes, cache_warmup_steps, sampling_strategy, seed_schedule, repeat_count.
Runner adapters: small shim for existing runners so they accept eval_config without changing internal runner logic (keep runner plugin interface minimal).

Profile publishing: artifacts are zipped with metrics.json, runs.csv, manifest.json (provenance) and uploaded to s3://redwood-profiles/{model}/{version}/{profile_semver}/; registry index updated with signed entry pointing to artifact manifest.
Profile signing: use existing KMS flow for artifact signature; include sig metadata in registry index for integrity checks on replay.
progress_updates: 2025-02-10: Ticket created after spike with infra and research teams. Identified reproducibility gaps in dataset sampling.
2025-02-18: Prototype dataset manifest schema and local deterministic iterator working for small english QA dataset (Marco).
2025-02-24: Proof-of-concept stochastic scheduler that runs 5 repeats and aggregates p50/p90/p99 completed; initial results show reduced noise when repeat_count >= 15.
2025-03-01: Integration design doc posted; PR for eval_config schema opened (github.com/redwood-inference/harness/pull/412).
2025-03-04: Implemented manifest upload to staging S3 bucket and basic profile artifact packaging; need to wire KMS signing and CI gating next.
design_decisions: Persist canonical_seed per dataset split rather than globally. This keeps per-dataset reproducibility independent of other datasets.
Use repeat_count-based aggregation to compute confidence intervals instead of single-run p95 due to GPU variance on p99 measurements.
Keep eval runner adapter API intentionally small: runners read eval_config and write standardized run-metadata. We avoid forcing runners to change batching internals.
Semantic versioning for profiles: MAJOR for breaking sampling/schema changes, MINOR for significant dataset additions, PATCH for metadata or non-impacting additions.
Opted to sign profiles using KMS RSA signatures to ensure registry integrity and to support offline/private deployments validating profiles without KMS by storing public key.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large evaluation repeat counts increase GPU cost. Mitigation: add adaptive stopping based on confidence interval convergence and allow sampling budgets per model tier.
Risk: Tokenizer differences across model families cause tokenization drift. Mitigation: include tokenizer fingerprint in manifest and run tokenization-stability checks during linting.
Risk: Backwards compatibility with older runners. Mitigation: runner adapter layer with fallbacks and a deprecation schedule documented in the design doc.
Risk: Registry bloat from many profile versions. Mitigation: retention policy and automated consolidation jobs that mark older profiles archive and store cold copies.
qa_plan: Unit tests for deterministic iterators and manifest parsing (edge cases: empty splits, filters that reduce size to <batch_size).
Integration test: run small model against curated dataset with --replay flag and assert identical runs.csv content (ignoring timestamps) across two runs.
CI regression test: baseline profile stored in test-assets; new artifact must not regress p99 latency by >10% without explicit override.
Manual review: PM/Research validation of aggregated metrics and sanity-check prompts for hallucination-sensitive evals.
rollback_plan: If the profile publishing pipeline causes CI failures or incorrect profiles, revert to previous registry index and disable auto-publish job; run manual audit on the queued profile artifacts and re-publish only after fixes.
notes: Coordinate with Platform SRE for S3 lifecycle policies and KMS grants for the harness service account.
Work with Developer Experience to expose --replay and --inspect flags in the CLI for easier debugging by PMs and model owners.
Follow-up ticket suggested: expose per-profile token-cost breakdown and tokenization diff reports (ENG-35012 suggested).
